content_voiceover: This is a real printed light transmission aggregometry report, paired with lumiaggregometry, so optical aggregation and ATP release are measured simultaneously from the same sample. The agonist is arachidonic acid at 0.5 millimolar. Traces one and two show a brisk response, sixty-nine percent amplitude aggregation with a slope of 94 and a lag time under a minute, plus 1.16 nanomoles of ATP secreted, confirming intact dense granule release. Traces three and four are essentially flat, zero percent amplitude, zero slope, lag time over ten minutes, meaning no aggregation and no ATP secretion to arachidonic acid. Arachidonic acid is the classic agonist boards use to probe the cyclooxygenase-thromboxane pathway directly, bypassing surface receptors, so an absent response points to a COX-1 defect. That's exactly the pattern seen with aspirin or another irreversible COX-1 inhibitor, and it's the textbook way LTA detects aspirin effect.
keypoints: AA-induced LTA = go-to test for aspirin/COX-1 defect
Trace 1-2: normal, 69% amplitude, ATP release 1.16 nmol
Trace 3-4: flat, 0% amplitude, no ATP release
Lumiaggregometry = optical + ATP (dense granule) in one run
